title: 🔥 Jesus and the Children: The Chosen’s Most Beautiful Lie Yet
paragraphs:
🔥 Jesus and the Children: The Chosen’s Most Beautiful Lie Yet
(The Chosen – Season 1, Episode 3: “Jesus Loves the Little Children”)

A group of children find a humble carpenter in the woods.
He jokes with them.
He plays games.
He builds toys.
He laughs at their questions and teaches them gently.

It’s emotional. It’s adorable.
It’s... wrong?

At first glance, it feels harmless—even beautiful.
But under the surface is a dangerous rebranding of the Messiah:
A Jesus who entertains more than He equips.
A Christ who connects—but never corrects.
A version of Jesus that’s safe, sweet… and spiritually sanitized.

❓ READER QUESTION:
“Brother John, is it really wrong to show Jesus being tender with children? Isn’t that part of who He is?”

📖 MAIN BIBLE VERSE – Matthew 19:14 (KJV):
“But Jesus said, Suffer little children, and forbid them not, to come unto me: for of such is the kingdom of heaven.”

Yes—Jesus welcomed children.
Yes—He valued their childlike faith.
But nowhere in Scripture did He spend days playing with them, entertaining them, or crafting wooden toys to win their trust.

🔥 Jesus didn’t disciple kids with jokes.
🔥 He drew them with truth—and demanded faith.

🚨 THE TRUTH: What This Blog Will Reveal
✔️ What The Chosen adds emotionally—but deletes doctrinally
✔️ Why portraying Jesus as a camp counselor lowers His divine nature
✔️ How fiction opens the door for future deception
✔️ The true scriptural model for how Jesus viewed, spoke to, and used children to teach faith
✔️ Why this episode may be the most subtle deception of all

THE CORE TRUTH – WHAT DOES THE BIBLE SAY?
❓ READER QUESTION:
“Brother John, didn’t Jesus love children? Isn’t it okay to imagine what He might’ve been like with them?”

Yes… He loved them.
But He never lowered His glory to become a cartoon Messiah for toddlers.
There’s a difference between being gentle—and being downgraded.
Let’s break it down biblically.

📖 JESUS WELCOMED CHILDREN – BUT NEVER ENTERTAINED THEM
Matthew 18:2–3 (KJV):

“And Jesus called a little child unto him, and set him in the midst of them,
And said, Verily I say unto you, Except ye be converted, and become as little children,
ye shall not enter into the kingdom of heaven.”

🔥 Jesus used children to teach adults about conversion and humility.
He didn’t sit around whittling animals or telling jokes to win their affection.

📖 JESUS WAS FIRM—EVEN WITH YOUNG ONES
Luke 2:48–49 (KJV) – 12-year-old Jesus said:
“...wist ye not that I must be about my Father’s business?”

✔ Even as a child, Jesus had kingdom focus.
✔ He wasn't playful—He was purposeful.

💣 WHAT THE CHOSEN SHOWS IN EPISODE 3:
❌ A Jesus who lives in the woods, isolated, playing with children
❌ Telling stories, building toys, laughing, crafting lesson moments
❌ Soft-spoken and emotionally approachable, but never holy or feared

🚨 This is not the Jesus of Scripture.
This is a Disney-level rebrand of the Son of God.

📖 THE BIBLE WARNS ABOUT ALTERING JESUS’ IMAGE:
2 Corinthians 11:4 (KJV):
“For if he that cometh preacheth another Jesus… ye might well bear with him.”
Exodus 20:4 (KJV):
“Thou shalt not make unto thee any graven image…”
🔥 Recreating Jesus in our imagination—no matter how “wholesome”—violates the command to worship Him as He is, not as we wish He was.

💥 TRUTH DROP:
✔ Jesus never followed children around to gain their trust.
✔ Children were drawn to His presence because of His purity—not His personality.
✔ He never acted silly to relate to them—He spoke truth, even to their parents.
📖 Mark 10:15 (KJV):
“Whosoever shall not receive the kingdom of God as a little child, he shall not enter therein.”
💣 The power was in how they received Him, not how He acted around them.

BIBLICAL & HISTORICAL PROOF – WHAT THE EARLY CHURCH UNDERSTOOD ABOUT JESUS & CHILDREN
📖 JESUS SPOKE TO CHILDREN—but never as one of them
Mark 10:14 (KJV):
“Suffer the little children to come unto me, and forbid them not: for of such is the kingdom of God.”

✔ Jesus welcomed children.
✔ But He didn’t run after them or tell stories to entertain them.
✔ He drew them into His divine presence, not a playpen environment.

📖 JESUS PRAISED CHILDLIKE FAITH—but never acted childish
Matthew 21:16 (KJV):
“Out of the mouth of babes and sucklings thou hast perfected praise?”

🔥 The children praised Jesus in the temple.
They weren’t giggling around a campfire with Him.
They recognized His divinity and responded with pure worship.

💥 THE PROPHETIC JESUS – CHILDREN FEARED & WORSHIPED HIM
Isaiah 11:6–9 (KJV) – Messianic Prophecy:

“...and a little child shall lead them...
They shall not hurt nor destroy in all my holy mountain:
for the earth shall be full of the knowledge of the Lord…”

🔥 This prophecy speaks of a peaceful dominion, not playtime.
Children are safe in His Kingdom—not because He’s soft,
but because He’s righteous.

🏛️ EARLY CHURCH UNDERSTANDING – JESUS WAS HOLY, NOT HARMLESS
📜 JUSTIN MARTYR (c. 150 AD)
In his writings, children were taught to fear the Lord from a young age—not to see Jesus as a friend who makes wooden toys.
“We instruct our children to rise early and read the Scriptures… to obey the commandments of Jesus Christ who shall return to judge the living and the dead.”

✔ No jokes.
✔ No playtime theology.
✔ Just fear, faith, and fire.

📜 THE DIDACHE (c. 1st Century Teaching Manual)
“Let your children learn the fear of God from youth, and let them cling to righteousness…”
🔥 Early Christians taught children who Jesus was, not how to “relate” to Him emotionally.

📖 Ecclesiastes 12:1 (KJV):
“Remember now thy Creator in the days of thy youth…”
Children in Scripture are called to remember their Creator, not reimagine Him.

💣 THE REAL DANGER:
The Chosen’s version of Jesus turns Him into:

❌ A campfire mentor
❌ A gentle hobbyist
❌ A divine babysitter
🚨 This paves the way for a generation of youth who love a Jesus that never existed.

OLD TESTAMENT PROPHECY CONNECTIONS
❓ READER QUESTION:
“Brother John, doesn’t the Old Testament show that God loves children too?”
Absolutely. But let’s make one thing clear:

📖 God loved children,
But He never lowered His holiness to keep their attention.

📖 PROPHECY #1 – THE MESSIAH WOULD BE FEARED, EVEN BY CHILDREN
Malachi 1:14 (KJV):
“...For I am a great King, saith the Lord of hosts, and my name is dreadful among the heathen.”
🔥 Even children in biblical times were raised to fear the Lord, not to casually hang out with Him.

📖 PROPHECY #2 – THE KNOWLEDGE OF GOD WILL COVER THE EARTH
Isaiah 11:9 (KJV):
“...for the earth shall be full of the knowledge of the Lord, as the waters cover the sea.”

✔ The goal was never to make Jesus relatable—it was to make Him known.
✔ Children would grow up in a world saturated with His glory—not His personality.

📖 PROPHECY #3 – A CHILD SHALL LEAD THEM (BUT NOT ENTERTAIN THEM)
Isaiah 11:6 (KJV):
“...and a little child shall lead them.”

📌 This verse points to humility, purity, and trust,
Not playtime in a forest clearing.

📖 PROPHECY #4 – GOD REQUIRES FEAR FROM YOUTH
Ecclesiastes 12:1 (KJV):
“Remember now thy Creator in the days of thy youth…”

🔥 Children are called to remember, not reimagine.
They are called to fear, not to familiarize with the Divine.

💣 THE DANGER THE CHOSEN IGNORES:
When Jesus becomes a friend to children, but not their Lord,
We’ve built a Messiah in our own image.
🚨 That is how the Antichrist will be introduced—as someone everyone can relate to, especially the youth.
📖 Daniel 11:21 (KJV):
“...he shall come in peaceably, and obtain the kingdom by flatteries.”
🔥 JESUS DIDN’T COME TO FLATTER KIDS—HE CAME TO SAVE THEIR SOULS.

He didn’t build toy animals—He builds His Church.
He didn’t perform to be liked—He preached to be obeyed.

REAL-LIFE TESTIMONY – “I Didn’t Know I Was Leading My Son to a Fake Jesus”
❓ READER QUESTION:
“Brother John, does this kind of portrayal really affect children spiritually?”

🔥 TESTIMONY:
“When The Chosen came out, I was excited. I thought, ‘Finally, something safe for my kids.’
My youngest—Ezekiel, only 9 years old—watched Episode 3 five times. He laughed, he smiled, he loved ‘Jesus.’
But then one night during prayer, he asked me something I wasn’t ready for…
He said, ‘Mom, if Jesus is funny and nice and likes to play, why do people say He’s going to judge sinners? I don’t like that version. I like the one in the show.’

My heart dropped.
That’s when I realized… I had unknowingly introduced my son to another Jesus.
A Jesus who entertained but never confronted.
A Jesus who made you feel safe—but didn’t call you to surrender.

We stopped watching it.
We started reading the Gospels together, verse by verse.
And now?
My son knows the Jesus who flipped tables, wept over Jerusalem, healed lepers, and will return as Judge.
That’s the Jesus who saves. That’s the Jesus I want my children to know.”

📖 CONFIRMING SCRIPTURE:
John 10:27 (KJV):
“My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me.”
Proverbs 22:6 (KJV):
“Train up a child in the way he should go: and when he is old, he will not depart from it.”

💣 EMOTIONAL JESUS ISN’T ENOUGH.
Our children need to see the Jesus of power, truth, and glory—not just gentleness and laughter.

FINAL CHALLENGE – WILL YOU LET YOUR KIDS FOLLOW THE REAL JESUS OR THE RELATABLE ONE?
❓ READER QUESTION:
“Brother John, what’s the real danger of just letting kids enjoy a softer version of Jesus?”
The danger is eternal.

A child who grows up believing Jesus is just gentle, playful, and poetic—
…won’t be ready for the Jesus who comes in flaming fire to judge the nations (2 Thessalonians 1:8).
…won’t repent, because they were never told they needed to.
…won’t endure, because they were never taught that Christianity is war.

📖 WARNING FROM THE WORD:
Galatians 1:6–8 (KJV):

“I marvel that ye are so soon removed from him that called you into the grace of Christ unto another gospel:
Which is not another; but there be some that trouble you, and would pervert the gospel of Christ…
If any man preach any other gospel… let him be accursed.”

💣 The Chosen presents another Jesus
—relatable but not righteous,
—gentle but not glorious,
—approachable but not authoritative.
That’s not a gift. That’s a false gospel.

⚠️ ASK YOURSELF:
✔ Have I allowed media to paint a softer Jesus in my child’s heart?
✔ Does my home teach the Jesus of Matthew, Mark, Luke, and John—or the Jesus of Netflix?
✔ Am I raising warriors—or watchers?
📖 Luke 6:46 (KJV):
“And why call ye me, Lord, Lord, and do not the things which I say?”
🔥 FINAL WARNING:

A relatable Jesus won’t save them.
Only the biblical Jesus will.
🚨 If the Jesus your children admire doesn’t preach, command, rebuke, and reign—they are admiring an idol with a biblical name.

THE FOOL’S RESPONSE VS. THE WISE RESPONSE
📖 Proverbs 14:18 (KJV):
“The simple inherit folly: but the prudent are crowned with knowledge.”

❌ THE FOOL’S RESPONSE:
“Relax—it’s just for kids!”
“At least it’s better than worldly cartoons.”
“God knows our hearts—it’s the intention that matters.”
“You’re being too harsh. Let the children enjoy Jesus.”
“You're overthinking it—it’s not that deep.”

🔥 Fools want comfort, not conviction.
🔥 Fools want emotion, not edification.
🔥 Fools will trade truth for peace—and raise children unprepared for persecution.

✅ THE WISE RESPONSE:
“If it’s not in Scripture, I don’t want it shaping my children.”
“My family doesn’t need a media Messiah—we need the Jesus of the Bible.”
“I want my children to fear God, not just be fond of Him.”
“I’ll trade entertainment for eternity—every single time.”
“Let the Word be the only lens through which we teach our kids who Jesus is.”
📖 Matthew 7:24 (KJV):
“Therefore whosoever heareth these sayings of mine, and doeth them, I will liken him unto a wise man…”

🔥 The wise raise warriors, not watchers.
🔥 The wise choose truth—even when it’s not trending.

WHAT IF YOU DIED TONIGHT?
❓ READER QUESTION:
“Brother John, I know this show is just a tool… but why make it so serious?”

Because eternity is serious.
Because your soul is serious.
And because one day—maybe even tonight—you’ll stand before the real Jesus.

Not the smiling one from Episode 3.
Not the gentle teacher from the forest.
But the glorified King, with eyes of fire and a sharp two-edged sword coming from His mouth
(Revelation 1:14–16).
📖 Hebrews 9:27 (KJV):
“And as it is appointed unto men once to die, but after this the judgment.”
💣 If you died tonight…
Would you stand before the Jesus of Scripture or the Jesus of cinema?
Would He say “Well done”… or “I never knew you”?
Would your children recognize the real Christ—or only the character?

📖 Matthew 7:21–23 (KJV):
“Not every one that saith unto me, Lord, Lord, shall enter into the kingdom of heaven…
And then will I profess unto them, I never knew you: depart from me, ye that work iniquity.”
🔥 THIS ISN’T ABOUT A SHOW. THIS IS ABOUT YOUR SOUL.

✔ It’s not about what inspired you—it’s about what saved you.
✔ It’s not about what moved your emotions—it’s about what transformed your life.

📖 Romans 10:9 (KJV):
“That if thou shalt confess with thy mouth the Lord Jesus, and shalt believe in thine heart that God hath raised him from the dead, thou shalt be saved.”
🚨 If you haven’t surrendered to the biblical Jesus—do it now.

Turn off the screen.
Open the Bible.
Repent of sin.
Follow the Christ who saves, commands, and returns.

SATAN’S SNEAK ATTACKS – HOW EMOTION BECOMES DECEPTION
📖 2 Corinthians 11:14 (KJV):
“And no marvel; for Satan himself is transformed into an angel of light.”

❓ READER QUESTION:
“Brother John, are you saying The Chosen is demonic?”

Not every scene.
Not every actor.
But the strategy behind it? YES.

Because Satan’s most effective lie isn’t the horror movie…
…it’s the harmless one.
The beautiful one.
The one that looks and feels good, but leads people away from the real Jesus.

💣 SATAN’S STRATEGY #1 – MAKE JESUS RELATABLE, NOT REVERED
If Satan can turn Jesus into:

❌ A gentle storyteller
❌ A playful craftsman
❌ A calm forest friend of children
…then the fear of the Lord is gone, and the reverence dies.
📖 Psalm 111:10 (KJV):
“The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom…”

💣 SATAN’S STRATEGY #2 – TRAIN CHILDREN TO FOLLOW A COUNTERFEIT
Let the next generation grow up loving:

✔ The Jesus who laughs and plays
❌ But not the Jesus who judges and returns with wrath
✔ The Jesus who hugs
❌ But not the One who will rule with a rod of iron (Revelation 19:15)

💥 That’s not preparation.
That’s Antichrist grooming.

💣 SATAN’S STRATEGY #3 – GET PARENTS TO LOWER THEIR GUARD
He whispers:
“It’s better than worldly cartoons.”
“At least it mentions Jesus.”
“My kids are learning something.”
🔥 While slowly replacing Scripture with screenplays.
📖 Hosea 4:6 (KJV):
“My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge…”

💣 SATAN’S STRATEGY #4 – BUILD A JESUS EVERYONE LOVES
✔ The Antichrist won’t come as a tyrant.
✔ He will come as the savior the world wants.
📖 Daniel 11:21 (KJV):
“...he shall come in peaceably, and obtain the kingdom by flatteries.”
The groundwork is being laid by media like The Chosen.
🔥 WAKE UP, WARRIOR.

You don’t protect your child by filtering out worldly content…
…you protect them by filtering out false portrayals of Christ.

GOSPEL WARRIOR DECLARATION – THE FINAL STAND FOR TRUTH
❓ READER QUESTION:
“Brother John, I see the deception now. What should I do next?”

Don’t just agree. Declare.
Don’t just cry. Commit.
Don’t just like the blog—live the truth.

🛡️ SAY THIS OUT LOUD:
“Lord Jesus, I reject every false version of You.
I will not follow a fictional Messiah or a feel-good Jesus.
I surrender to the Jesus of Scripture—holy, righteous, glorious, and returning soon.
I will raise my family in truth.
I will protect the next generation from emotional deception.
I will follow You, even when it costs me everything.
I am not ashamed of the Gospel.
I AM A GOSPEL WARRIOR.
In Jesus’ mighty name, AMEN!”
